chapter: Touring abroad and the future of music
title: Herman's modest role and pride in young educators' approval
summary: He says his life has been about entertaining, not organizing, but is proud of young educators' approval.

story.theme_name: Late-career reflections: awards, legacy and life lessons
story.community_name: Looking back: no regrets, what it all meant

blocks.x: And if you just think about this for a moment, Herb, and I don't want to dwell on it, but my entire life has had nothing to do with getting people up to do anything. My whole life has been to entertain an audience, nothing more, nothing less, and be able to live with my own soul and the music I'm going to play anyway.

And spent my life with me, because that's where it's usually spent. So I'm not really a proper person, I haven't been built for this. But my pride has been tremendously strengthened by the approval of the young music educators.
And so I'm trying to put in my two cents.
But it's not because I feel that I could organize anything, other than build my own tune and let me off (inaudible).
Well, I think that there are a lot of these young music educators --
Yeah, and some of them are very good, and some of them are very dumb. But that's the law of averages
